title: Accounting Core: one economic world, many independent accounting truths
summary: Accounting Core is shared infrastructure, not a shared ledger. Each legal entity owns its own book and posts its own accounting consequence of authoritative operational evidence. A correlation can connect FlyLo, Federation, All Japan, VMM or other counterparties without granting cross-company posting authority. Banking, insurance, airline, market-making, tax and regulatory engines remain separate operational/policy authorities.
invariants: A legal entity owns an independent AccountingEngine and AccountingBook; shared software does not imply shared books.

Operational systems are authoritative for what happened; executable accounting policy decides what that evidence means to one legal entity; Accounting Core enforces posting mechanics and evidence binding.
A common economic correlation links evidence for reconciliation but never authorises one entity to write another entity's books.
The banking engine is not the accounting engine, and a bank-account balance is not a substitute for a legal entity's general ledger.
The core is intentionally boring: jurisdiction-specific tax law, exotic ownership structures and regulator rules belong in versioned policy/evidence layers.
procedure: When entering a new project, identify each legal entity that needs its own accounting truth before designing journals or reports.
Load the accounting-rigour companion sphere when implementing arithmetic, persistence, replay or rounding-sensitive behaviour.

provenance.claim: Accounting Core is shared infrastructure, not a shared ledger; each legal entity owns independent accounting truth and policy maps operational evidence into that truth.
